name: Dallas Smith
editorial_article:
Dallas Hendry Smith (born December 4, 1977) is a Canadian singer-songwriter who successfully transitioned from a career as the frontman of the hard rock/post-grunge band Default to becoming one of Canada's most prominent solo country artists. Born in New Westminster and raised in Langley, British Columbia, Smith first achieved international recognition with Default in the early 2000s, scoring hits like "Wasting My Time." In 2011, he launched his solo career with the album "Jumped Right In," embracing a modern country-rock sound produced largely by Joey Moi.

Smith has become a dominant force on Canadian country radio, holding the record for the most number-one singles by a male Canadian artist on the Billboard Canada Country chart. His work, including albums such as "Side Effects" and "Timeless," bridged the gap between his rock roots and contemporary country pop sensibilities, often featuring polished, anthemic production. Throughout his tenure in the industry, Smith has received numerous accolades, including multiple Canadian Country Music Association (CCMA) awards, cementing his status as a key figure in modern Canadian country music. He remains an active performer and a recognizable voice, maintaining a career defined by versatility and consistent radio success. His evolution from a hard rock vocalist to a country crossover superstar highlights a rare adaptability in the music industry, and he continues to influence the sound of modern Canadian country music today.
